message.content: In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is regarded as the central figure—often seen as the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy and the ultimate revelation of God’s plan for humanity. However, the importance of other prophets such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and John the Baptist is also emphasized in Scripture, each playing distinct roles in the unfolding narrative of salvation history. Different Christian traditions may highlight various aspects of these figures, so perspectives on who is “most important” can vary among believers.
